$comment: Declares the harness as a machine-readable graph. In v2 this graph was scattered across markdown tables and prose, making it impossible to verify or instrument, and as a result 'a declared but unreachable asset' (rules/, 697 lines) went undiscovered by anyone for 4 months. doctor --graph uses this file to check for dangling edges, unreachable nodes, and missing error edges. instrumented:true on an edge means a hook actually emits it. Edges between stages are model behavior and cannot be emitted by code, so they are excluded from the 'dead edge' decision. A node's phase links this graph to the Phase vocabulary in rules/workflow-routing.md (P0-A~E, P1~P6) — if the two vocabularies diverge, routing becomes machine-uncheckable. A node's produces is attached only to 'artifacts the harness reads again later' — an artifact that is delivered to the user and ends there (a marketing site, a favicon) is not a store. A store node must have both inbound (write) and outbound (read) edges: a store with no reader is pure cost and a source of drift. A node's beforeWrite declares that a skill 'must be called before the first write to that path' — the prior-knowledge gate of security-check reads only this (when: test-runner = only when a test runner exists). It is the only place that hangs a sentence of the routing card on the execution path.
